memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Abraham was now very old, and the LORD had blessed him in every way. He said to the senior servant in his household, the one in charge of all that he had, 'Put your hand under my thigh. I want you to swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living, but will go to my country and my own relatives and get a wife for my son Isaac.'" - Gen 24:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham is old now, and one thing weighs on his heart more than his wealth or his cattle — the future of his son. Isaac must marry, and Abraham will not leave that decision to chance. He does not want a wife from among the Canaanites, whose gods and ways would pull the family away from the living God. So he sends his most trusted servant back to his own people to find a wife who shares the family's faith.

Notice what matters to Abraham. God had blessed him in every way, yet his concern is not comfort but covenant. He remembers that through Isaac, God had promised to bring blessing to all nations — the promise that would one day lead to Christ (Gal 3:16). A godly marriage was part of guarding that promise.

For us, this is a quiet reminder that our biggest decisions — who we marry, where we settle, how we raise our children — deserve prayer and care, not carelessness. Whom we walk closely with shapes whom we become. Abraham teaches us to think about the next generation and to value shared faith above outward attractions.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What decisions am I leaving to chance that actually deserve prayerful care?
2. Do I value shared faith in my closest relationships?
3. How am I guarding the faith of the next generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to bring my big decisions to You and to treasure a shared love for You above every other quality. Guide me and those I love toward faithfulness. Amen.
